meta.name: Extract drug discovery intelligence with Claude, Voyage AI, Pinecone, Airtable and Slack

name: AI Drug Discovery Literature Intelligence Pipeline

parameters.content:
## AI Drug Discovery Literature Intelligence Pipeline

Every run, this pulls newly published journal articles, preprints, patent filings, and clinical trial updates, uses Claude to extract structured R&D intelligence (drug targets, molecules, mechanisms of action, development stage, competing organizations) from each one, scores each finding for novelty/strategic relevance, and writes it into a searchable database - both a structured table (Airtable) for filtering and a vector index (Pinecone) for semantic search. High-value discoveries (first-in-class mechanisms, novel targets in your watch list) trigger an immediate Slack alert to the R&D team; everything else is silently indexed. A run digest is posted at the end either way.

### How to set up
1. Import this workflow into n8n
2. Add credentials: PubMed/NCBI E-utilities (API key optional but recommended), bioRxiv/medRxiv API, a patents API (e.g. PatentsView, Lens.org, or Google Patents via SerpApi), ClinicalTrials.gov API, Voyage AI, Pinecone, Anthropic, Airtable, and Slack
3. Edit Set - Config: search keywords/therapeutic areas, watchTargets list, API base URLs, Airtable base/table IDs, Pinecone index/namespace, Slack channel, noveltyThreshold
4. Point the Airtable and Pinecone nodes at your actual base/index
5. Activate the workflow, or use the Manual Trigger to test end to end

### How to customize
- Add more sources (e.g. FDA Orange Book, company press releases) as extra parallel HTTP Request nodes feeding the same Merge node
- Adjust the novelty-scoring logic and watch-list matching in Code 3
- Swap Airtable for Postgres/Notion, or Pinecone for another vector store, by changing just the upsert nodes
- Wire the Slack alert to also open a ClickUp/Jira research-review task

## 1. Trigger & Data Collection

Set - Config centralizes every API URL, search keyword list, watch list, and destination (Airtable/Pinecone/Slack) config.

Four parallel HTTP Request nodes pull freshly published material:
- HTTP Request - Fetch PubMed Publications (journal articles)
- HTTP Request - Fetch bioRxiv/medRxiv Preprints
- HTTP Request - Fetch Patent Filings (new drug-related patent applications/grants)
- HTTP Request - Fetch Clinical Trials Updates (new/updated trial registrations)

Merge - Combine All Sources joins all four into one item per run. Code 1 then normalizes every source into a single document shape and dedupes against previously seen documents (title/DOI/patent-number hash, tracked via workflow static data), emitting one item per new, unseen document.

## 2. Per-Document AI Extraction & Scoring (looped)

Split In Batches processes one new document at a time so each Claude call stays focused and cheap.

For each document: API 1 (HTTP Request) sends the title/abstract/claims text to Claude with a strict extraction prompt - drug targets, molecules, mechanism of action, indication, development stage, competing organizations, and whether it looks first-in-class. Code 2 parses that JSON. Code 3 scores novelty/strategic relevance by combining Claude's own assessment with a match against your configured watch list of targets and therapeutic areas.

Every document then gets embedded (API 2 - Voyage AI) and upserted into Pinecone (API 3) for semantic search, plus written as a structured row into Airtable - so the database is searchable both by free-text similarity and by filterable fields (target, stage, source type, date).

IF - High-Value Discovery Gate branches only the *notification*: high-scoring finds get an immediate Slack alert; everything else is indexed silently. Both paths loop back into Split In Batches until every new document for this run has been processed.

## 3. Run Digest

Once Split In Batches has no more documents left (the 'done' output), Code 4 builds a summary of the run - how many new documents were found, how many were high-value, and a short list of the top discoveries - which is posted to Slack as a daily digest for the research team, independent of any individual alerts sent during the loop.

parameters.jsonBody:
={{ JSON.stringify({ model: 'claude-sonnet-4-6', max_tokens: 1200, system: 'You are a pharmaceutical R&D intelligence analyst. Read the given document (journal article, preprint, patent, or clinical trial record) and extract structured drug-discovery intelligence. Respond ONLY with valid JSON, no prose, matching exactly this shape: {"drugTargets": string[], "molecules": string[], "mechanismOfAction": string, "indication": string, "developmentStage": string, "competingOrganizations": string[], "isFirstInClass": boolean, "noveltyNotes": string, "summary": string}. If a field cannot be determined, use an empty string, empty array, or false.', messages: [ { role: 'user', content: 'Source type: ' + $json.sourceType + '
Title: ' + $json.title + '
URL: ' + ($json.url || 'n/a') + '
Text:
' + ($json.abstractOrClaims || '').slice(0, 4000) } ] }) }}

={{ JSON.stringify({ namespace: $('Code 3 - Score Novelty & Strategic Relevance').first().json.pineconeNamespace, vectors: [ { id: $('Code 3 - Score Novelty & Strategic Relevance').first().json.dedupeKey, values: $json.data[0].embedding, metadata: { title: $('Code 3 - Score Novelty & Strategic Relevance').first().json.title, sourceType: $('Code 3 - Score Novelty & Strategic Relevance').first().json.sourceType, url: $('Code 3 - Score Novelty & Strategic Relevance').first().json.url, relevanceScore: $('Code 3 - Score Novelty & Strategic Relevance').first().json.relevanceScore, summary: $('Code 3 - Score Novelty & Strategic Relevance').first().json.summary } } ] }) }}
